episodes.title: Inside Turkey’s Infamous Cult: How It Led to an 8,658-Year Prison Sentence | True Crime
episodes.description:
Our Hindi Channel-https://youtube.com/@kvhindi-l7i?si=HpKNuOyqOC3-ZCrm

Adnan Oktar, Turkey’s infamous cult leader, built one of the country’s most disturbing and bizarre high-control groups before receiving an extraordinary 8,658-year prison sentence. But how did Adnan Oktar gain such extraordinary control over his followers—and why did so many people remain inside his world for years?
In this true crime deep dive, Dr. D, a professor and lawyer, and Sam, a counselor, explore the rise and fall of Adnan Oktar and his cult, examining the case through psychology, law, history and Steven Hassan’s BITE Model of Authoritarian Control.
We look closely at cult psychology, coercive control, manipulation, indoctrination, recruitment, dependency, isolation and cult deprogramming, asking one of the most difficult questions surrounding high-control groups: how can intelligent, educated people gradually surrender control over enormous parts of their lives to a charismatic leader?
But the story of Adnan Oktar cannot be understood without understanding Turkey itself. We also take a crash course through modern Turkish history, secularism, religion and politics, examining the social and political conditions in which Oktar’s movement developed and expanded.
This episode of Kollectively Vigilant combines true crime, psychology and law to examine not simply what Adnan Oktar did, but how a cult like his was able to exist in the first place.
If you are interested in true crime documentaries, cult documentaries, criminal psychology, cult leaders, coercive control, the BITE Model, deprogramming, Turkish history and the psychology of manipulation, this episode is for you.

Dr. D — Professor & Lawyer
Sam — Counselor and HIgh School Teacher

episodes.title: The Kenyan Starvation Cult: Paul Mackenzie and the Shakahola Mass Graves- Season 2 Episode 4
episodes.description:
In 2023, authorities in Kenya uncovered mass graves in the Shakahola Forest, exposing one of the deadliest cult cases in modern African history.
Paul Mackenzie, leader of the Good News International Church, is accused of instructing followers to starve themselves and their children in order to “meet Jesus.” Hundreds of bodies were recovered from shallow graves in a forest compound.
Mackenzie and several associates now face multiple criminal charges in connection with the deaths.
In this episode, we examine:
• The structure of the cult
• The legal charges filed against its leader
• Criminal liability in coercive religious movements
• State oversight failures
• The tension between religious freedom and criminal accountability
This is a case study in mass manipulation, institutional breakdown, and preventable tragedy.
Kollectively Vigilant: Law and Crime.
